translationRepairs: He was assigned to the Southern Study and Maqin Hall, and was promoted to grand preceptor.
He was assigned to the Southern Study and Maqin Hall, and was promoted to supervisor of the Heir Apparent’s Household.
s0008 has 遷詹事; 詹事 heads the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent and is not 太師 (grand preceptor). The replacement restores the correct Qing office title.
He served in the Southern Study and the Maqin Hall, and was transferred to grand preceptor.
He served in the Southern Study and the Maqin Hall, and was transferred to supervisor of the Heir Apparent’s Household.
s0008 has 遷詹事; 詹事 is supervisor of the Heir Apparent’s Household, not grand preceptor. The literal’s “grand preceptor” is a false office title.
He was promoted in succession to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
He was promoted in succession to academician of the Grand Secretariat.
s0036 has 累遷內閣學士; 內閣學士 is an academician of the Grand Secretariat, distinct from 大學士 (grand secretary). The prior wording elevates the rank incorrectly.
He was repeatedly promoted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
He was repeatedly promoted to academician of the Grand Secretariat.
s0036 has 累遷內閣學士; translating it as grand secretary confuses 學士 with 大學士. Academician of the Grand Secretariat matches the Chinese.
He rose in succession to Hanlin expositor, minister of the Imperial Stud, and grand secretary, while retaining his educational post.
He rose in succession to Hanlin reader academician, minister of the Imperial Stud, and academician of the Grand Secretariat, while retaining his educational post.
s0102 has 侍讀學士、太僕寺卿、內閣學士; 侍讀學士 is a reader academician (not expositor, which is 侍講學士), and 內閣學士 is academician, not grand secretary.
He was repeatedly promoted to expositor of the Hanlin Academy, minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat, retaining his educational post throughout.

He was repeatedly promoted to reader academician of the Hanlin Academy, minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and academician of the Grand Secretariat, retaining his educational post throughout.
s0102 lists 侍讀學士 and 內閣學士; the literal wrongly renders them as Hanlin expositor and grand secretary. Reader academician and academician of the Grand Secretariat are accurate.
He was promoted in succession to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
He was promoted in succession to academician of the Grand Secretariat.
s0143 has 累遷內閣學士; this is academician of the Grand Secretariat, not grand secretary (大學士).
He was repeatedly promoted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
He was repeatedly promoted to academician of the Grand Secretariat.
s0143 has 累遷內閣學士; the literal’s “grand secretary” misidentifies the office. Academician of the Grand Secretariat is correct.
In year 6, when mourning ended, he acted as vice-minister of Rites and Works and of granary stores, again served in the Upper Study, and instructed the eldest imperial son Yizhi.
In year 6, when mourning ended, he acted as vice-minister of Rites and Works and of granary stores, again served in the Upper Study, and instructed the eldest imperial son Yiwei.
s0173 has 授皇長子奕緯讀; 奕緯 romanizes as Yiwei, not Yizhi. The proposed name correction matches the Chinese characters.
In the sixth year, when mourning ended, he acted as vice-minister of Rites and Works and of the granary stores, again served in the Upper Study, and instructed the eldest imperial son Yizhi.
In the sixth year, when mourning ended, he acted as vice-minister of Rites and Works and of the granary stores, again served in the Upper Study, and instructed the eldest imperial son Yiwei.
s0173 has 奕緯; 緯 is wei, so Yiwei is required. Yizhi invents a different personal name.
